transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-12
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Participants: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (DataLight Eng Mgr), Priya Kapoor (DataLight SRE), Ethan Moore (DataLight Platform)
Links referenced: pilot-runbook.docx (shared), filtered-logs (link), benchmarks.xlsx (partial)

Summary: Quick follow-up after last week's reliability incidents (timeouts, intermittent 5xxs). Confirmed root-candidate hypotheses (rate-limiting + retry storms), agreed on short-term mitigations and next steps for a longer synthetic load test and extended logging.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight - 45 minutes on the calendar, i know you had some follow up from the incident on tuesday
[00:18] Jordan: yeah thanks, uh appreciate you fitting us in, Priya's got the tl;dr on what we saw
[00:24] Priya: ok so, recap - between 08:12 and 08:28 UTC we saw a spike in 5xxs, timeouts on the inference endpoint, primarily for long-context requests, and then a secondary spike about 09:03 when retry storms hit after our client retries kicked in
[00:40] Liam: got it, did you see any regular pattern in seq len or model variant?
[00:46] Priya: mostly the 8k seq jobs, the model was the rwd-xxl-v2 (and sometimes the rwd-xxl-v2-quant), but there were a handful of shortcode requests as well, it's messy
[00:58] Ethan: we also had a rate limit hit on our side, the client lib returned 429 and we attempted exponential backoff but the backoff jitter was low so a lot retried around the same cadence
[01:12] Maya: ok so two likely contributors - server-side saturation on larger sequences and client-side retry behavior causing bursts. Did you also see any errors in KV cache or the fronting proxy?
[01:25] Priya: there were some proxy 502s but logs show connection resets; the log lines call it "KV cash" in one place which i think is a transcription of KV cache, so not confident about wording there
[01:35] Jordan: yeah and our ops noticed the firewall between VPC subnets was re-evaluating sessions - might be unrelated but it lined up
[01:42] Liam: ok; a couple of quick notes from the Redwood SE perspective - we've seen the same pattern in other pilots: 1) longer sequences increase compute path time and block batching, 2) if client retries don't back off with enough jitter you can create self-inflicted load, 3) transient 5xx can be from kernel OOM or queue saturation on the host
[02:05] Priya: do you have visibility into kernel-level OOMs? we didn't see OOM killer logs on our side
[02:12] Liam: we can pull the node logs and provide kernel messages, yes. earlier in the incident we did record some unusually long scheduling waits on the host that align with the 5xx window
[02:23] Maya: also worth noting we had a configuration on the Redwood Dedicated pool where the autoscaler threshold was a bit conservative - we have a fix that reduces scale delay from 120s to 45s in the config we propose for the pilot
[02:39] Ethan: would that help mid-burst? if autoscaler is slower we still get queued work and more timeouts
[02:45] Liam: it helps for sustained bursts, but not for immediate retry storms. For immediate mitigation we recommend 1) increase client-side backoff/jitter, 2) implement 429 handling to slow down, 3) temporarily raise request concurrency quota so the runtime doesn't reject while we scale
[03:10] Jordan: can you do a short list of config deltas we'll need to apply? the team can flip flags in our staging cluster
[03:18] Maya: yes, we'll send a delta list - autoscaler timing, concurrency quota bump, and an optional per-route soft-queue limit. we'll also include an updated guidance doc for retry best practices (exponential backoff with randomized jitter, capped retries)
[03:35] Priya: on the logs, some of the request ids map to internal test traffic, so we'll filter those before sharing, but we'll try to include a few full traces where the 5xx occurred
[03:48] Liam: we'll also instrument additional metrics on the runtime - queue length, host-sched-wait, kv-cache hit ratio, and kernel-messages. that should help correlate if it's a kernel-level issue or a runtime queueing problem
[04:05] Ethan: curious about quotas - if we temporarily raise concurrency quota does that change billing or pilot limits?
[04:12] Maya: for the pilot we can grant a temporary quota increase without changing the billing, we'll note usage and if needed propose a short-term commit for dedicated capacity if you want predictable throughput
[04:30] Jordan: good, and on the legal/data front we still need the data residency note for any retained logs - our compliance team is picky about egress of identifiers
[04:40] Maya: understood, we'll redact PII, use request-level ids, and note retention windows in the runbook excerpt we share
[04:50] Priya: one more question - any change in model variant that would be less memory hungry but similar perf? we tried the quant variant but saw slightly higher latencies in some cases
[04:58] Liam: we have a couple of mid-sized variants (rwd-xl-plus) that have lower memory demands and similar quality for many prompts; we'll provide a quick comparison table
[05:10] Maya: ok team, to recap - Liam will send logs and kernel messages, Priya will share runbook excerpts and dashboards, Maya to send pricing and config delta, Jordan will confirm stakeholders. we'll run a planned load test on 2026-05-18 and follow up 2026-05-19. any other blockers?
[05:28] Jordan: nope that's it, thanks everyone
[05:31] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc links

End of transcript
